changes.after: Keep an old search answer from replacing the answer to a newer search.

before: A search can start before an earlier search finishes. Responses may arrive in the opposite order from their requests. If an old response is displayed just because it arrived last, it can replace the answer the user currently wants. A request id is a number assigned when a request starts; keep the largest, newest id so the program can identify current work.

Use let for the newest id and the visible text because they change. Start the id at zero, then use `latestId++` to add one for each search. A Set holds canceled ids without duplicates. `.add(id)` records one, and `.has(id)` checks membership. Marking an old id canceled is bookkeeping in this fixture; it does not stop a real network operation.

The guard contains two questions joined by `&&`, meaning both must be true. The strict equality asks whether the result belongs to the newest id. The exclamation mark `!` means not, so `!cancelledIds.has(id)` asks whether it has not been canceled. The function only assigns visibleResult inside this guard. A stale result leaves the current text alone.

For real browser fetch work, an AbortController can request cancellation. Create a controller, pass its `.signal` in fetch's options, and call `.abort()` when the work becomes outdated. The request can reject with an abort error. Cancellation may arrive after completion, and stopping the client does not prove the server did no work. Keep the id guard as well. The supplied exercise models cancellation using a set rather than making actual fetch calls.

In your exercise, oldId must be smaller than newId. Mark oldId canceled when starting the new request, display "new answer", and ignore "old answer" even when it arrives afterward. Arrival time does not change which request is current. Tests should vary response order and confirm that stale text never overwrites current text. The canceled-id set grows in this small fixture; a long-running application could remove entries once the old work can no longer return.
after:
Search answers can arrive out of order. A slow old search might finish after a newer one.

Give each search an ID when it starts. Keep the newest ID so the page can tell which answer still matters.

`latestId` starts at zero. Increase it by one for each new search.

A `Set` stores canceled IDs without duplicates. `add(id)` records one, and `has(id)` checks for it. In this exercise, marking an ID canceled does not stop real network work.

The guard checks two things: the answer's ID matches `latestId`, and it is not in `cancelledIds`.

`&&` requires both checks to pass. `!` means not. Only then should `receiveResult` change `visibleResult`.

For real requests, `AbortController` can ask unfinished work to stop. Pass its `signal` to `fetch`, then call `abort()` when the request is outdated.

Keep the ID check too. Cancellation might come too late, and stopping a client request does not undo work already done by a server. Our exercise uses fixed answers instead of network requests.

Add `const cancelledIds = new Set()` to the starter. Complete `beginSearch` so it marks the previous ID canceled, increases `latestId`, and returns the new ID.

Complete `receiveResult` with the two checks. The starter must keep `new answer` visible after `old answer` arrives.

This small example keeps old IDs in the Set. A long-running app should remove records once they are no longer needed.

before: Each call to `beginSearch` should increment and return the id.
In `receiveResult`, compare the response id with `latestId`.
Only assign to `visibleResult` when the ids match.
after: Declare cancelledIds before the search calls.
Use id === latestId && !cancelledIds.has(id) before updating visibleResult.

project.title: A responsive search tool
project.task: Track search IDs and ignore outdated answers. Add a cancelledIds Set, complete beginSearch, and update visibleResult only for the latest uncanceled ID.
project.done_when: New IDs increase, replaced requests are marked canceled, and old answers never overwrite the current result.
